2. The present respondent No. 2, Abdul Khaleque Chowdhury as petitioner filed the aforesaid writ petition challenging the legality of Memo No. Je: Pro:/Cox/SA/7-19/2009/ 2175 dated 23-11-2009 stating, inter alia, that 7.27 acres of land of Khatian No. 1, Plot No. 2262 originally belonged to Abdul Bari Peshker and the said Abdul Bari Peshker while owning and possessing the same died leaving behind four sons namely, Fazlul Karim, Bazlur Rahim, Abu Bakar Siddique and Abu Teher. The MRR Khatian was accordingly prepared in their names. Abu Bakar Siddique, subsequently sold out 88 decimals of land out of the said 7.27 acres of land (hereinafter referred to as the case land) by an unregistered sale deed dated 7-7-1969 and delivered possession thereof to the writ petitioner. The writ petitioner while enjoying the case land on paying rent to the Government, it had gone under river Bankkhali and lost by diluvion during the year 1971- 1972. Thereafter, the case land was recorded in the name of the Deputy Commissioner, Cox's Bazar under Khatian No. 1 as Plot No. 2262. Subsequently, 54.04 acres of land including the case land re-appeared in situ by alluvion between the years 1995 to 2000 and became cultivable. In 2000, Abdul Khaleque Chowdhury made an application for leasing out the said 54.04 acres of land including the case land in his favour. Upon inquiry, the Tashilder of Union Land Office, Cox's Bazar submitted a report on 12-9-2000 to the Assistant Commissioner (Land), Sadar, Cox's Bazar mentioning that the land had become cultivable. Whereupon, the Assistant Commissioner recommended for placing the said application to the "Shrimp Mahal Committee" for consideration. Thereupon, the writ petitioner made a representation on 5-10-2000 to the concerned authority for allotment of the case land in his favour. But it was kept in abeyance. So, the writ petitioner filed another application for allotment of case land under section 86 of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act, 1950 (shortly, the SA&T Act) as amended by Act No. 15 of 1994 (hereinafter referred to as the Amending Act). The concerned authority i.e. the Deputy Commissioner and District Collector, Cox's Bazar rejected the said application by Memo dated 23-11-2009., Abdul Khaleque Chowdhury thereafter filed Writ Petition No. 98 of 2010 and obtained a rule. 

 4. Whereupon, the Deputy Commissioner and District Collector of Cox's Bazar filed Civil Petition for Leave to Appeal No. 2120 of 2011 before this Division contending, inter alia, that in the writ petition, it is admitted by the writ petitioner that the land in question was lost by diluvion during the years 1971-1972 and re-appeared in situ between the years 1995 to 2000 and, as such, the land did not re-appear within a period of 30 years and for which all right, title and interest in the said land by the previous tenants extinguished. So, it was rightly recorded in the name of the Government in Khatian No. 1, Plot No. 2262. The writ petitioner has no legal right to get allotment of the land in question. The amended provision of section 86(1) of the SA&T Act came into operation on 13th July, 1994 by the Amending Act and no retrospective affect was given to the said amended provisions and therefore, the writ petitioner cannot claim the benefit of section 86 of the Amending Act. 

 6. The present appellants as third parties-petitioners filed civil review petition No. 507 of 2018 for reviewing the judgment and order passed by this Division in the aforesaid civil petition contending, inter alia, that they are legal heirs of original MRR Khatian tenant/ owner Bazlur Rahim. They, as plaintiffs, filed Other Class Suit No. 42 of 2012 on 27-2-2012 in the 1st Court of Joint District Judge, Cox's Bazar against the Deputy Commissioner, Cox's Bazar and two others praying for declaration of title to the land of Khatian No. 1, in respect of 14.40 acres of land appertaining to plot Nos. 2270, 2271, 2272, 2273, 2262, 2269, 10002 and 10003 which includes 0.88 acres of land of Plot No. 2262 of Khatian No. 1, mentioned as the case land in Writ Petition No. 98 of 2010. In that suit it was mentioned that the suit land was wrongly recorded in the name of Government and that defendant Nos. 1 and 2 threatened the plaintiffs to dispossess from the suit land. They also filed an application for temporary injunction to restrain the defendants from leasing out the suit land to anybody else and from dispossessing the plaintiffs therefrom. The prayer for injunction was allowed by order No. 18 dated 6-3-2013. 

 25. From the review petition it appears that the present appellants as legal heirs of original MRR Khatian tenant/owner Bazlur Rahim filed Other Class Suit No. 42 of 2012 on 27-2-2012 in the 1st Court of Joint District Judge, Cox's Bazar against the Deputy Commissioner, Cox's Bazar and two others praying for declaration of title to the land of Khatian No. 1, in respect of 14.40 acres of land appertaining to plot Nos. 2270, 2271, 2272, 2273, 2262, 2269, 10002 and 10003, which includes 0.88 acres of land of Plot No. 2262 of Khatian No. 1, mentioned as the case land in Writ Petition No. 98 of 2010.
